head: b7ee4555810dcb82b4a0714200c599ab076daac8
summary: Maintainers can ask the agent to merge an approved revision when no required checks exist. The bounded exception preserves other merge gates; authorization remains agent-enforced, and measured savings are unknown.
reasons: Issue #551 demonstrates an unnecessary manual merge step after Ask approval. The change restores the existing approved-merge outcome without requiring maintainers to configure artificial checks.

The 12-file change adds one head-bound exception, result evidence, setup guidance, and focused tests without new dependencies or configuration. Existing required-check discovery and other merge gates remain in place.
Ask authorization remains agent-enforced, consistent with the existing merge-authority boundary. Ruby verifies the confirmed head rather than claiming to verify user approval.

Three local review rounds and hosted repairs do not establish an approach problem. Detailed repair history, incident frequency, measured time savings, and full instruction-growth report output are unavailable; the supplied instruction estimate is about 30 workflow words.
alternative: Keep the existing GitHub merge click. It preserves native safeguards but loses agent completion after explicit Ask approval—the demonstrated workflow gap. Requiring a configured check would impose a repository policy change to solve that gap.
next_action: Carry this change forward with the existing human review requirement for merge-guard changes.
